She'd pin her ears every time the saddle came out. Crow-hopped when asked to move off. Her owner in DFW had tried everything — different saddle pad, different warm-up, a month of ground work.

Dr. Leo found it on the first visit. Locked up through the mid-back. One session, and the mare that acted like she hated her job started acting like herself again.

Attitude problems that show up consistently at the same moment in the routine almost always have a physical root. Horses don't pin their ears to be difficult.

If your horse is telling you something, it's worth listening.

DM us to book — Dr. Leo is working across North Texas.

The horses that hold up through the back half of the season are the ones that got maintained during it — not just before it started.

If your horse has been hauling and running since spring across North Texas or up into the Great Falls area, July is exactly the right time to let Dr. Leo put hands on him. Not because something is obviously wrong. Because something small caught early doesn't become something expensive caught late.

Mobile. Dr. Leo comes to your barn. You don't haul a sore horse anywhere.

Slots are moving. DM 'BOOK' to grab one, or book now at shortgochiro.com.
